children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised:
What is being said?

children.text: yadi vinā rūpādyarthena rūpādivijñaptirutpadyate na rūpādyarthāt ||
children.translated_text: If the cognition of form and so on arises without an external object such as form and so on, and not from an object such as form and so on,
why does it arise in some place and not everywhere?

children.text: tatraiva ca deśe kadācidutpadyate na sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: And why does it arise at some time in that very place, and not always?

children.text: taddeśakālapratiṣṭhitānāṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃtāna utpadyate na kevalamekasya ||
children.translated_text: Why does it arise in the continua of all those established in that place and time, and not merely in one person's?
For example, the appearance of hairs and the like occurs in the continua of those with eye disease, but not in others.

children.text: kasmādyattaimirikaiḥ keśabhramarādi dṛśyate tena keśādikriyā na kriyate na ca tadanyairna kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Why is the activity of hairs and the like not performed by the hairs, flies, and so on that are seen by those with eye disease, and why is it not the case that it is not performed by other things?

children.text: yad annapānavastraviṣāyudhādi svapne dṛśyate tenānnādikriyā na kriyate na ca tadanyairna kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Why is the activity of food and the like not performed by the food, drink, clothing, poison, weapons, and so on that are seen in a dream, and why is it not the case that it is not performed by other things?

children.text: gandharvanagareṇāsattvān nagarakriyā na kriyate na ca tadanyairna kriyate tasmādasad yad bhāvanābhāsane deśakālaniyamaḥ saṃtānāniyamaḥ kṛtyakriyā ca na yujyate ||
children.translated_text: By a city of the <s>gandharvas</s>, because it is unreal, the activity of a city is not performed, and it is not the case that it is not performed by other things. Therefore, if it is nonexistent, the restriction of place and time in the appearance of an impression, the absence of restriction to one continuum, and the performance of an effect are not coherent.
They are certainly not incoherent, because:
As in a dream, like a dream.
How, to begin with?

children.text: svapne vināpyarthena kvacideva deśe kiṃcid bhramarārāmastrīpuruṣādikaṃ dṛśyate na sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a dream, even without an object, some thing such as a bee, a park, a woman, or a man is seen only in a certain place, not everywhere.

children.text: tatraiva ca deśe kadācid dṛśyate na sarvakālamiti siddho vināpyarthena deśakālaniyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in that very place it is seen at some time, not at all times. Thus the restriction of place and time is established even without an object.

children.text: siddha iti vartate pretānāmiva pretavat kathaṃ siddhaḥ samam ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'it is established' continues. As for pretas, like pretas: how is it established equally?
A river full of pus is a pus-river.
Like a pot of ghee.

children.text: tulyakarmavipākāvasthā hi pretāḥ sarve'pi pūyapūrṇāṃ nadīṃ paśyanti naika eva ||
children.translated_text: For pretas whose karmic maturation is in the same condition all see a river full of pus; it is not one alone.
By the expression 'and so on' it is understood that, just as it is full of pus, it is also full of urine, feces, and the like, and occupied by men holding sticks and swords.
Thus the non-restriction to a single continuum of cognitions is established even when there is no object.
It should be understood as established.
As in the hells, like hell.
How is it established?

children.text: yathā hi narakeṣu nārakāṇāṃ narakapālādidarśanaṃ deśakālaniyamena siddhaṃ śvavāyasāyasaparvatādyāgamanagamanadarśanaṃ cetyādigrahaṇena sarveṣāṃ ca naikasyaiva taiśca tadbādhanaṃ siddhamasatsvapi narakapālādiṣu samānasvakarmavipākādhipatyāt ||
children.translated_text: For just as, in the hells, the vision by hell-beings of hell-wardens and the like is established with restriction of place and time, and, through the expression 'and so on,' the vision of dogs, crows, iron mountains, and the like coming and going is also included; and this belongs to all of them, not to only one; and their being tormented by these is established, even though hell-wardens and the like do not exist, because of the predominance of the similar maturation of their own karma.

children.text: tathānyatrāpi sarvam etad deśakālaniyamādicatuṣṭayaṃ siddhamiti veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: So too elsewhere all this fourfold set, beginning with restriction of place and time, should be understood as established.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ narakapālāste ca śvāno vāyasāśca sattvā neṣyante ||
children.translated_text: But for what reason are the hell-wardens, and those dogs and crows, not accepted as sentient beings?
Because that is not possible.
For they cannot be hell-beings.
Since, in that same way, they do not experience that suffering.

children.text: parasparaṃ yātayatāmime nārakā ime narakapālā iti vyavasthā na syāt ||
children.translated_text: There would be no distinction such as, 'these are the hell-beings and these are the hell-wardens,' when they torment one another.

children.text: tulyākṛtipramāṇabalānāṃ ca parasparaṃ yātayatāṃ na tathā bhayaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And if they were equal in form, size, and strength while tormenting one another, there would not be fear in the same way.

children.text: dāhaduḥkhaṃ ca pradīptāyāmayomayyāṃ bhūmāvasahamānāḥ kathaṃ tatra parānyātayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And, unable to endure the burning pain on a blazing iron ground, how could they torment others there?
Or, if they are not hell-beings, how could they arise in hell?
How, then, is there arising of animals in heaven?

children.text: evaṃ narakeṣu tiryakpretaviśeṣāṇāṃ narakapālādīnāṃ saṃbhavaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In this way, in the hells, there could be the arising of special animals or pretas, namely hell-wardens and the like.

children.text: ye hi tiryañcaḥ svarge sambhavanti te tadbhājanalokasukhasaṃvartanīyena karmaṇā tatra sambhūtās tajjaṃ sukhaṃ pratyanubhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For the animals that arise in heaven have arisen there through karma leading to the happiness of that container-world, and they experience the happiness born there.

children.text: na caivaṃ narakapālādayo nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavanti ||
children.translated_text: But hell-wardens and the like do not in this way experience hellish suffering.

children.text: tasmānna tiraścāṃ saṃbhavo yukto nāpi pretānām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the arising of animals is not reasonable, nor that of pretas.

children.text: teṣāṃ tarhi nārakāṇāṃ karmabhistatra bhūtaviśeṣāḥ sambhavanti varṇākṛtipramāṇabalaviśiṣṭā ye narakapālādisaṃjñāṃ pratilabhante ||
children.translated_text: Then, through the karma of those hell-beings, special elements arise there, distinguished by color, shape, size, and strength, which receive the designation 'hell-wardens' and so on.

children.text: tathā ca pariṇamanti yad vividhāṃ hastavikṣepādikriyāṃ kurvanto dṛśyante bhayotpādanārthāṃ yathā meṣākṛtayaḥ parvatā āgacchanto gacchanto 'yaḥśālmalīvane ca kaṇṭakā adhomukhībhavanta ūrdhvamukhībhavantaśceti ||
children.translated_text: And they transform in such a way that they are seen performing various actions such as movements of the hands, intended to produce fear, just as mountains having the shape of rams come and go, and in the forest of iron <s>śālmalī</s> trees the thorns turn downward and upward.
It is not that these do not arise at all.

children.text: vijñānasyaiva tatkarmabhistathā pariṇāmaḥ kasmānneṣyate kiṃ punarbhūtāni kalpyante ||
children.translated_text: Why is it not accepted that consciousness itself transforms in that way through those karmas? Why, instead, are elements imagined?
Moreover:

children.text: yena hi karmaṇā nārakāṇāṃ tatra tādṛśo bhūtānāṃ saṃbhavaḥ kalpyate pariṇāmaśca tasya karmaṇo vāsanā teṣāṃ vijñānasaṃtānasaṃniviṣṭā nānyatra ||
children.translated_text: The impression of the karma by which the arising and transformation of such elements there for the hell-beings is imagined is lodged in the continua of their consciousness, not elsewhere.

children.text: yatraiva ca vāsanā tatraiva tasyāḥ phalaṃ tādṛśo vijñānapariṇāmaḥ kiṃ neṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And where the impression itself is, why is its result, a transformation of consciousness of that kind, not accepted there itself?

children.text: yatra vāsanā nāsti tatra tasyāḥ phalaṃ kalpyata iti kimatra kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: What reason is there here for imagining its result where the impression is not?
Scripture is the reason.

children.text: yadi vijñānam evaṃrūpādi pratibhāsaṃ syānna rūpādiko'rthastadā rūpādyāyatanāstitvaṃ bhagavatā noktaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: If consciousness had an appearance of form and the like in this way, and there were no object such as form and the like, then the existence of sense-fields such as form would not have been taught by the <s>Bhagavat</s>.
This is not a reason, because:
Just as it was taught by the <s>Bhagavat</s>, 'There is a being that is born apparitionally.'
On account of intention, with reference to the non-interruption of the mental continuum in the future.
Because of this statement.

children.text: evaṃ rūpādyāyatanāstitvamapyuktaṃ bhagavatā taddeśanāvineyajanam adhikṛtyetyābhiprāyikaṃ tadvacanam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the existence of the sense bases such as form was also stated by the Blessed One with reference to the people to be trained by that teaching; that statement is therefore intentional.
What is the intention here?
What is being said?

children.text: rūpapratibhāsā vijñaptiryataḥ svabījātpariṇāmaviśeṣaprāptād utpadyate tacca bījaṃ yatpratibhāsā ca sā te tasyā vijñapteś cakṣūrūpāyatanatvena yathākramaṃ bhagavānabravīt ||
children.translated_text: The cognition that appears as form arises from its own seed when that seed has reached a particular transformation. The Blessed One spoke of that seed and of that appearance, respectively, as the eye sense base and the form sense base of that cognition.

children.text: evaṃ yāvat spraṣṭavyapratibhāsā vijñaptiryataḥ svabījāt pariṇāmaviśeṣaprāptād utpadyate ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, up to the cognition that appears as something tangible, which arises from its own seed when that seed has reached a particular transformation.

children.text: tacca bījaṃ yatpratibhāsā ca sā te tasyāḥ kāyaspraṣṭavyāyatanatvena yathākramaṃ bhagavānabravīd ityayamabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One spoke of that seed and of that appearance, respectively, as the body sense base and the tangible sense base of that cognition: this is the intended meaning.
But what advantage is there in teaching in this way, under the force of such an intention?
For, when it is taught in that way, they enter into the selflessness of persons.
From the pair the sixfold group of cognitions proceeds.

children.text: na tu kaścideko draṣṭāsti na yāvanmantetyeva viditvā ye pudgalanairātmyadeśanāvineyās te pudgalanairātmyaṃ praviśanti ||
children.translated_text: But there is no single seer, and so on up to no single thinker. Knowing just this, those who are to be trained by the teaching on the selflessness of persons enter into the selflessness of persons.
Alternatively, how is there entrance into the selflessness of dharmas through the teaching of mere cognition?

children.text: vijñaptimātramidaṃ rūpādidharmapratibhāsam utpadyate na tu rūpādilakṣaṇo dharmaḥ ko'pyastīti viditvā ||
children.translated_text: By knowing that this mere cognition arises with the appearance of dharmas such as form, but that no dharma at all exists with the defining character of form and the like.

children.text: yadi tarhi sarvathā dharmo nāsti tadapi vijñaptimātraṃ nāstīti kathaṃ tarhi vyavasthāpyate ||
children.translated_text: If, then, there is in every way no dharma, then mere cognition also does not exist. How, then, is it established?

children.text: na khalu sarvathā dharmo nāstītyeva dharmanairātmyapraveśo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Certainly entrance into the selflessness of dharmas does not occur simply by thinking that there is in every way no dharma.
Rather:

children.text: yo bālairdharmāṇāṃ svabhāvo grāhyagrāhakādiḥ parikalpitastena kalpitenātmanā teṣāṃ nairātmyaṃ na tv anabhilāpyenātmanā yo buddhānāṃ viṣaya iti ||
children.translated_text: The selflessness of those dharmas is in respect to the imagined self-nature, such as object grasped and grasper, which fools construct for dharmas; it is not in respect to the inexpressible nature that is the domain of the Buddhas.

children.text: evaṃ vijñaptimātrasyāpi vijñaptyantaraparikalpitenātmanā nairātmyapraveśāt vijñaptimātravyavasthāpanayā sarvadharmāṇāṃ nairātmyapraveśo bhavati na tu tadastitvāpavādāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because one enters into the selflessness even of mere cognition with respect to a self imagined by another cognition, the establishment of mere cognition brings about entrance into the selflessness of all dharmas, not the denial of their existence.

children.text: itarathā hi vijñapterapi vijñaptyantaramarthaḥ syāditi vijñaptimātratvaṃ na sidhyetārthavatītvād vijñaptīnām ||
children.translated_text: For otherwise another cognition too would be the object of a cognition, and mere-cognition-hood would not be established, since cognitions would possess objects.

children.text: kathaṃ punaridaṃ pratyetavyamanenābhiprāyeṇa bhagavatā rūpādyāyatanāstitvam uktaṃ na punaḥ santyeva tāni yāni rūpādivijñaptīnāṃ pratyekaṃ viṣayībhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: But how is it to be accepted that the Blessed One stated the existence of sense bases such as form with this intention, and not that those things really exist which become the separate objects of cognitions such as form-cognitions?
Because:
Thus.
What is being said?

children.text: yattadrūpādikamāyatanaṃ rūpādivijñaptīnāṃ pratyekaṃ viṣayaḥ syāttadekaṃ vā syādyathāvayavirūpaṃ kalpyate vaiśeṣikaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That sense base such as form, which would be the separate object of cognitions such as form-cognitions, would have to be either one, as the Vaiśeṣikas imagine the form that is a whole made of parts,
or many, atom by atom,
or those very atoms when aggregated.
First, it is not a single object, because nowhere is a whole form apprehended apart from its parts.
Nor is it many, because the atoms are not apprehended individually.
Nor do those atoms when aggregated become objects.
For an atom is not established as a single substance.
How is it not established?
Because:

children.text: ṣaḍbhyo digbhyaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ paramāṇubhiryugapadyoge sati paramāṇoḥ ṣaḍaṃśatā prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: If an atom is simultaneously joined by six atoms from the six directions, the atom would have six parts.
For where the region of one exists, another cannot possibly exist there.

children.text: atha ya evaikasya paramāṇordeśaḥ sa eva ṣaṇṇām ||
children.translated_text: But if the very same region of one atom is also the region of all six,

children.text: tena sarveṣāṃ samānadeśatvātsarvaḥ piṇḍaḥ paramāṇumātraḥ syātparasparavyatirekāditi na kaścitpiṇḍo dṛśyaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: then, since they all have the same location and are not distinct from one another, the whole mass would be only the size of an atom, and no mass at all would be visible.
Indeed atoms do not join together at all, because they are partless.
Let this unwanted consequence not arise.

children.text: saṃhatāstu parasparaṃ saṃyujyanta iti kāśmīravaibhāṣikāsta idaṃ praṣṭavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Kāśmīra-Vaibhāṣikas say instead that aggregates join with one another; they should be asked this:

children.text: yaḥ paramāṇūnāṃ saṃghāto na sa tebhyo'rthāntaramiti ||
children.translated_text: Is the aggregate of atoms something other than those atoms, or not?
The discussion concerns conjunction.
If aggregates too do not join with one another,

children.text: na tarhi paramāṇūnāṃ niravayavatvātsaṃyogo na sidhyatīti vaktavyam ||
children.translated_text: then it should not be said that conjunction is not established because atoms are partless.
For conjunction is not admitted even for an aggregate that has parts.
Therefore an atom is not established as a single substance.

children.text: yadi ca paramāṇoḥ saṃyoga iṣyate yadi vā neṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And whether conjunction of atoms is accepted or not accepted,

children.text: anyo hi paramāṇoḥ pūrvadigbhāgo yāvadadhodigbhāga iti digbhāgabhede sati kathaṃ tadātmakasya paramāṇorekatvaṃ yokṣyate ||
children.translated_text: the eastern-direction part of an atom is different, and so on up to its downward-direction part; when there is difference among directional parts, how will the unity of an atom whose nature is these be joined together?

children.text: yadyekaikasya paramāṇordigbhāgabhedo na syādādityodaye kathamanyatra chāyā bhavatyanyatrātapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If each single atom had no difference of directional parts, then when the sun rises, how could there be shadow in one place and sunlight in another?

children.text: na hi tasyānyaḥ pradeśo'sti yatrātapo na syāt ||
children.translated_text: For it has no other region where sunlight would not be present.

children.text: āvaraṇaṃ ca kathaṃ bhavati paramāṇoḥ paramāṇvantareṇa yadi digbhāgabhedo neṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And how could there be obstruction of one atom by another atom, if difference of directional parts is not accepted?
For there is no part at all of an atom
that is a far side, where, because another does not arrive, one thing's resistance to another could occur.

children.text: asati ca pratighāte sarveṣāṃ samānadeśatvātsarvaḥ saṃghātaḥ paramāṇumātraḥ syādityuktam ||
children.translated_text: And if there is no resistance, then, since all have the same location, the whole aggregate would be only the size of an atom, as has been said.

children.text: kimevaṃ neṣyate piṇḍasya te chāyāvṛtī na paramāṇoriti ||
children.translated_text: Is this not accepted: that shadow and covering belong to your mass, not to the atom?

children.text: kiṃ khalu paramāṇubhyo'nyaḥ piṇḍa iṣyate yasya te syātām ||
children.translated_text: Is a mass really accepted as something other than the atoms, to which those two would belong?
He says: no.

children.text: yadi nānyaḥ paramāṇubhyaḥ piṇḍa iṣyate na te tasyeti siddhaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If no mass other than the atoms is accepted, then it is established that those two do not belong to it.
This is only an imagined arrangement.
Or else one says, 'an atom' or 'an aggregate.'
What is the use of this reflection?

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ tu rūpādi yadi na pratiṣidhyate ||
children.translated_text: But if the defining mark, such as color-form and the rest, is not denied,

children.text: kiṃ punasteṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cakṣurādiviṣayatvaṃ nīlāditvaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: then what is their defining mark? Is it being the object of the eye and so on, and being blue and so on?
That very point is now being examined.

children.text: yattaccakṣurādīnāṃ viṣayo nīlapītādikamiṣyate kiṃ tadekaṃ dravyamatha vā tadanekamiti ||
children.translated_text: That which is accepted as the object of the eye and the other faculties, blue, yellow, and so forth: is it one substance, or is it many?
What follows from this?
The fault in its being many has been stated.

children.text: yadi yāvad avicchinnaṃ nānekaṃ cakṣuṣo viṣayastadekaṃ dravyaṃ kalpyate pṛthivyāṃ krameṇetirna syādgamanamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, so far as it is uninterrupted, what is not many and is the eye's object is imagined to be one substance, then there would be no movement step by step on the earth; this is the meaning.
For by setting down the foot once, all of it would have been traversed.

children.text: arvāgbhāgasya ca grahaṇaṃ parabhāgasya cāgrahaṇaṃ yugapan na syāt ||
children.translated_text: And the apprehension of the near part and the non-apprehension of the far part could not occur simultaneously.

children.text: na hi tasyaiva tadidānīṃ grahaṇaṃ cāgrahaṇaṃ ca yuktam ||
children.translated_text: For it is not reasonable that the very same thing should now be both apprehended and not apprehended.

children.text: vicchinnasya cānekasya hastyaśvādikasyānekatra vṛttirna syādyatraiva hyekaṃ tatraivāparamiti kathaṃ tayorviccheda iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And an interrupted, multiple thing such as elephants and horses would not occur in more than one place; for where one is, there the other would also be. How, then, is separation between them accepted?

children.text: kathaṃ vā tadekaṃ yatprāptaṃ ca tābhyāṃ na ca prāptamantarāle tacchūnyagrahaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Or how is that one thing which is reached by those two, and yet not reached in the interval, since the empty interval is apprehended?

children.text: sūkṣmāṇāṃ caudakajantūnāṃ sthūlaiḥ samānarūpāṇāmanīkṣaṇaṃ na syāt ||
children.translated_text: And tiny aquatic creatures having the same appearance as large ones would not fail to be seen.
If distinctness as another substance is imagined only because of a difference in defining mark, and not otherwise,
therefore difference must necessarily be imagined atom by atom.
And that single atom is not established.

children.text: tasyāsiddhau rūpādīnāṃ cakṣurādiviṣayatvam asiddhamiti siddhaṃ vijñaptimātraṃ bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: When it is not established, the being of color-form and the rest as objects of the eye and other faculties is not established; thus <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (cognition-only) is established.

children.text: pramāṇavaśādastitvaṃ nāstitvaṃ vā nirdhāryate sarveṣāṃ ca pramāṇānāṃ pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ gariṣṭham ityasatyarthe kathamiyaṃ buddhirbhavati pratyakṣamiti ||
children.translated_text: Existence or non-existence is determined by the force of a means of knowledge, and among all means of knowledge direct perception is the weightiest. If there is no object, how does this cognition arise: 'This is direct perception'?
It has already been explained that this occurs even without an object.

children.text: yadā ca sā pratyakṣabuddhirbhavatīdaṃ me pratyakṣamiti tadā na so'rtho dṛśyate manovijñānenaiva paricchedāccakṣurvijñānasya ca tadā niruddhatvāditi ||
children.translated_text: And when that cognition of direct perception occurs, 'This is directly perceived by me,' that object is not then seen, because it is determined only by mental consciousness and because the eye-consciousness has then ceased.
How, then, is its direct perceptibility accepted?

children.text: viśeṣeṇa tu kṣaṇikasya viṣayasya tad idānīṃ niruddhameva tadrūpaṃ rasādikaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Especially in the case of a momentary object, that color-form, taste, and so on has just then ceased.

children.text: nānanubhūtaṃ manovijñānena smaryata ityavaśyamarthānubhavena bhavitavyaṃ tacca darśanamityevaṃ tadviṣayasya rūpādeḥ pratyakṣatvaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: It is held that what has not been experienced is not remembered by mental consciousness; therefore there must be an experience of an object, and that is seeing. In this way the direct perceptibility of its object, color-form and so forth, is considered.
This is not established: that there is memory of an experienced object.
Because:

children.text: vināpyarthena yathārthābhāsā cakṣurvijñānādikā vijñaptir utpadyate tathoktam ||
children.translated_text: Just as a cognition such as eye-consciousness, having the appearance of an object, arises even without an object, so it has been stated.

children.text: tato hi vijñapteḥ smṛtisamprayuktā tatpratibhāsaiva rūpādivikalpikā manovijñaptir utpadyata iti na smṛtyutpādādarthānubhavaḥ sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: From that cognition there arises a mental cognition, associated with memory, having that same appearance and constructing color-form and the rest; therefore the experience of an object is not established from the arising of memory.

children.text: yadi yathā svapne vijñaptirabhūtārthaviṣayā tathā jāgrato'pi syāttathaiva tadabhāvaṃ lokaḥ svayamavagacchet ||
children.translated_text: If cognition in a dream has a non-existent object, and it were likewise so for one who is awake, then in the same way people would themselves recognize that object's absence.
But this does not happen.
Therefore, not all apprehension of objects is objectless as in a dream.
This does not prove the point.
Because:

children.text: evaṃ vitathavikalpābhyāsavāsanānidrayā prasupto lokaḥ svapna ivābhūtamarthaṃ paśyanna prabuddhastadabhāvaṃ yathāvannāvagacchati ||
children.translated_text: People, asleep as it were through the sleep of habituated impressions of false constructions in this way, see a non-existent object as in a dream and, not being awakened, do not correctly understand its absence.

children.text: yadā tu tatpratipakṣalokottaranirvikalpajñānalābhāt prabuddho bhavati tadā tatpṛṣṭhalabdhaśuddhalaukikajñānasaṃmukhībhāvād viṣayābhāvaṃ yathāvad avagacchatīti samānametat ||
children.translated_text: But when they are awakened by obtaining supramundane non-conceptual knowledge that is opposed to it, then, through the manifestation of pure worldly knowledge obtained subsequently to that, they correctly understand the absence of objects. Thus the case is the same.

children.text: yadi svasaṃtānapariṇāmaviśeṣād eva sattvānām arthapratibhāsā vijñaptaya utpadyante nārthaviśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: If cognitions that appear as objects arise for beings only from a particular transformation of their own continuum, and not from a particular external object,

children.text: tadā ya eṣa pāpakalyāṇamitrasaṃparkāt sadasaddharmaśravaṇācca vijñaptiniyamaḥ sattvānāṃ sa kathaṃ sidhyati asati sadasatsaṃparke taddeśanāyāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: then how is the regularity of cognition among beings established, which comes from contact with bad and good friends and from hearing true and false dharma, if there is no contact with good and bad persons and no teaching of that?

children.text: sarveṣāṃ hi sattvānāmanyonyavijñaptyādhipatyena mitho vijñapterniyamo bhavati yathāyogam ||
children.translated_text: For all beings, according as is appropriate, have a regularity of cognition mutually through the dominance of one another's cognitions.
'Mutually' means from one another.

children.text: ataḥ saṃtānāntaravijñaptiviśeṣāt saṃtānāntare vijñaptiviśeṣa utpadyate nārthaviśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, from a particular cognition in another continuum, a particular cognition arises in another continuum, not from a particular external object.

children.text: yadi yathā svapne nirarthikā vijñaptirevaṃ jāgrato 'pi svāt kasmāt kuśalākuśalasamudācāre suptāsuptayostulyaṃ phalamiṣṭāniṣṭam āyatyāṃ na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If, just as in a dream, cognition is objectless, and it is so also for one awake, why is the pleasant or unpleasant result in the future not accepted as the same for one asleep and one not asleep when wholesome or unwholesome conduct occurs?
Because:
This is the reason here, not the real existence of an object.

children.text: yadi vijñaptimātramevedaṃ na kasyacitkāyo 'sti na vāk ||
children.translated_text: If this is nothing but <s>vijñaptimātra</s>, and no one's body or speech exists,

children.text: katham upakramyamāṇānām aurabhrikādibhir urabhrādīnāṃ maraṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: how does the death of sheep and the like occur when they are attacked by sheep-butchers and the like?

children.text: atatkṛte vā tanmaraṇe kathamaurabhrikādīnāṃ prāṇātipātāvadyena yogo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or, if their death is not caused by them, how are sheep-butchers and the like connected with the fault of taking life?
For just as, through the mental power of demons and the like, other people undergo such alterations as loss of memory, dream-visions, and possession by spirits,
and also through the mental power of one who has supernatural ability,
as in the dream-vision of <s>Sāraṇa</s> through the direction of the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>,
and as the defeat of <s>Vemacitra</s> resulted from the corruption of the mind of forest sages,

children.text: tathā paravijñaptiviśeṣādhipatyāt pareṣāṃ jīvitendriyavirodhinī kācidvikriyotpadyate yayā sabhāgasaṃtativicchedākhyaṃ maraṇaṃ bhavatīti veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: so too, because of the dominance of a special cognition belonging to another, a certain alteration hostile to the life-faculty of others arises; by it there is what is called the cutting off of the continuity of the same class, namely death. This should be understood.
If it is not accepted that beings die because of the dominance of a special cognition belonging to another,

children.text: manodaṇḍasya hi mahāsāvadyatvaṃ sādhayatā bhagavatopālirgṛhapatiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, when the Blessed One was establishing that the mental rod is extremely blameworthy, the householder <s>Upāli</s> was asked:

children.text: kaccitte gṛhapate śrutaṃ kena tāni daṇḍakāraṇyāni mātaṅgāraṇyāni kaliṅgāraṇyāni śūnyāni medhyībhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: 'Householder, have you heard by what means those <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests, <s>Mātaṅga</s> forests, and <s>Kaliṅga</s> forests became empty and purified?'
He said:

children.text: śrutaṃ me bho gautama ṛṣīṇāṃ manaḥpradoṣeṇeti ||
children.translated_text: 'I have heard, sir <s>Gautama</s>, that it was through the corruption of the sages' minds.'
If it is supposed as follows:

children.text: tadabhiprasannair amānuṣaistadvāsinaḥ sattvā utsāditā na tvṛṣīṇāṃ manaḥpradoṣānmṛtā ityevaṃ sati kathaṃ tena karmaṇā manodaṇḍaḥ kāyavāgdaṇḍābhyāṃ mahāvadyatamaḥ siddho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: 'The beings dwelling there were destroyed by non-human beings who were greatly pleased by that corruption, but they did not die through the corruption of the sages' minds,' then, if this is so, how is the mental rod proven by that action to be more greatly blameworthy than the bodily and verbal rods?
It is proven from the death of so many beings through the mere corruption of those minds.

children.text: yadi vijñaptimātramevedaṃ paracittavidaḥ kiṃ paracittaṃ jānantyatha na ||
children.translated_text: If this is only cognition, do those who know another's mind know another's mind, or do they not?
What follows from that?

children.text: yadi na jānanti kathaṃ paracittavido bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: If they do not know it, how are they knowers of another's mind?
But if they do know it,
how is that also not according to reality?
Just as that, in its inexpressible nature, is the domain of the buddhas,

children.text: tathā tadajñānāttadubhayaṃ na yathārthaṃ vitathapratibhāsatayā grāhyagrāhakavikalpasyāprahīṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: so, because they do not know that, both are not according to reality, since they appear falsely and since the construction of grasped object and grasper has not been abandoned.
In the mind-only nature, whose divisions of endless determinations are unfathomably profound,

children.text: sarvaprakārā tu sā mādṛśaiścintayituṃ na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: it cannot, in all its modes, be thought out by people such as myself,
because it is not an object of reasoning.

children.text: kasya punaḥ sā sarvathā gocara ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Then whose domain is it in every respect? He says:

children.text: buddhānāṃ hi sā bhagavatāṃ sarvaprakāraṃ gocaraḥ sarvākārasarvajñeyajñānāvighātāditi ||
children.translated_text: For it is, in every mode, the domain of the blessed buddhas, because their knowledge of all knowable things in all aspects is unobstructed.
The Twenty Verses, the proof of mind-only.
This is the work of the teacher <s>Vasubandhu</s>.
